title: Stand-up Comedy — Pilot Articles
verification: Official uploader identities and timestamped captions checked in the browser. No independent acoustic timing or gesture audit. Clip timestamps are approximate locators; mechanism interpretations are editorial analysis.

patterns.title: Misdirection
use_when: The audience can predict the obvious ending.
An observation contains a plausible second interpretation.
The draft explains the joke before the audience can discover it.

sources.title: Mitch Hedberg — The Reason We Can't Find Big Foot

patterns.editorial_decision: New stand-up-specific draft; no existing same-title article found in the corpus.
patterns.distinction: Focuses on a listener's initial inference and revised reading; reversal is a related outcome structure.

visual.implementation: Markdown table contrasting initial reading with the information that changes it.
visual.rationale: The interpretive relationship is clearer than a decorative illustration.

example_user_queries: People can see my punchline coming.
My joke surprises people but the ending feels random.
How do I make an audience assume the wrong thing?
My setup gives away the funny part too early.
I have an observation but it reads like an explanation.
How can one sentence mean something different after the next line?
The reveal needs too much explanation to make sense.
I want a twist that fits what I already told the audience.

patterns.title: Add Tags
use_when: One punchline works but the passage ends immediately afterward.
An act-out establishes a relationship with unexplored comic possibilities.
Follow-up lines explain rather than develop the original joke.

sources.title: Mitch Hedberg — I Wish They Made Fajita Cologne
Taylor Tomlinson's PSA on Arm Floaties

patterns.editorial_decision: New draft using one compact receipt passage and one metaphor-based act-out; versions are not combined.
patterns.distinction: A tag supplies another payoff using established context; heightening increases scale or stakes, and a new scene may require another setup.

visual.implementation: Labeled original setup, punchline, weak continuation, and two candidate tags.
visual.rationale: A compact worked score demonstrates the difference between explanation and another payoff.

example_user_queries: I have one good punchline and then nothing else.
How do I get more material out of a joke that already works?
My follow-up line just explains why the joke is funny.
I keep starting over with a new setup after every laugh.
There is more in this character interaction but I cannot find it.
How do I know when an extra line makes a bit weaker?
I want to extend an act-out without repeating the same idea.
Are these extra lines still part of the joke or a new scene?

patterns.title: Let the Audience Finish
use_when: An established sequence makes the next implication sufficiently clear.
The final spoken line seems to explain what the audience already understood.
A performer's response to an implication may carry more than stating it.

sources.title: Eddie Izzard — On Advertising, from Unrepeatable
Mitch Hedberg — The Reason We Can't Find Big Foot

patterns.editorial_decision: New draft distinguishes a genuinely unspoken implication from a later spoken completion; no unverified gesture descriptions added.
patterns.distinction: A gap carries an inferable conclusion; an ordinary suspense pause still needs its final words, while a tag should add another payoff.

visual.implementation: Markdown table mapping established rule, revealing case, and deliberate gap to what remains unstated.
visual.rationale: Shows the informational sequence without inventing a universal timing prescription.

example_user_queries: People laugh before I finish the sentence.
The last line makes the joke feel overexplained.
How can a look or a silence do the work of a punchline?
My pause looks like I forgot what to say.
I want the audience to work out the implication themselves.
When should I leave the ending of a joke unspoken?
Does the audience need to guess the exact word I left out?
Should I say the punchline after people have already understood it?
